name: vlang vpm
recipe: N/A — cannot run standalone in the wasm32-wasi sandbox.
smoke: N/A. Would-be smoke (`vpm install pcre`) cannot execute: vpm's clone path calls os.execute_opt("git clone --recursive --filter=blob:none <url> <path>") and first probes os.find_abs_path_of_executable("git") — both require spawning a child process, which the sandbox forbids.
blocker: fork-exec: vpm's entire fetch mechanism spawns the external git/hg binary via os.execute_opt() (cmd/tools/vpm/vcs.v clone(); install.v also runs `git -C status`/`rev-list`). No internal HTTP client — network IS delegated to the spawned VCS process, so even shimmed net/fs cannot substitute. Secondary: V compiles to C (no plain wasm32-wasi target) and a self-hosted vpm would drag the V toolchain. Tool purpose = network git fetch.

name: wasm-pack
recipe: No viable recipe. wasm-pack is a pure fork-exec orchestrator with zero standalone-function value: it spawns `cargo`/`rustc` to compile Rust to wasm32-unknown-unknown (cdylib + wasm-bindgen proc-macro derive), invokes the native `wasm-bindgen` CLI to emit JS/TS glue, downloads `wasm-bindgen`/`wasm-opt` binaries over the network, and runs `wasm-pack test` via geckodriver/headless browsers. It then writes pkg/ npm dirs and calls npm pack/publish. Under wasmtime wasm32-wasi there is no spawn, no network-for-purpose, no browser — so the tool degenerates to nothing. The payload it builds also needs real rustc (proc-macros, edition) which mrustc~1.74 cannot do (Lane C dead too). To get wasm output we already have the in-sandbox Rust lane (mrustc->clang, compiler-in-wasm done); wasm-pack's orchestration role is replaced by that pipeline, not ported.
smoke: N/A — cannot run. If forced: `wasm-pack build` immediately calls execvp("cargo",...) which returns ENOSYS/ENOEXEC under WASI (no process model), and even stubbed it then needs network fetch of wasm-bindgen + a browser for `test`. No pure invocation produces useful output.
blocker: fork-exec orchestration: spawns cargo/rustc + wasm-bindgen CLI, downloads toolchain binaries over network, and runs headless browsers for tests — none available under wasm32-wasi/wasmtime. No standalone pure-function value remains; the Rust payload it builds also exceeds mrustc (proc-macro/edition).

name: GNU ld / gold
recipe: N/A — no viable lane. Lane B blocked: binutils ships no plain wasm32-wasi amalgam; it requires GNU autotools `configure` to generate config.h + per-target BFD tables (bfd-in2.h, targmatch, archures) which we cannot run in-sandbox. BFD pervasively assumes a hosted POSIX host (mmap, file descriptors, getpwuid) and uses dlopen for the LTO plugin path — wasi-libc has no dlopen. gold is C++ and explicitly pthread-multithreaded (parallel symbol resolution workqueue), which is a hard native-threads blocker. Not Lane A (no prebuilt plain wasm32-wasi .wasm exists), not C/D.
smoke: If it were ever buildable: echo 'int main(){return 0;}' compiled to a .o, then `wasmtime ld.wasm -o a.out crt1.o main.o -lc` should link and exit 0. Cannot be attempted — no buildable artifact.
blocker: gold = explicit native pthread multithreading (hard blocker). ld = GNU autotools configure-generated BFD/target config (no pregenerated amalgam) + hosted-POSIX/mmap/dlopen assumptions wasi-libc cannot satisfy. Also functionally redundant: LLVM lld (the wasm-native linker) is already LIVE and is what the existing C/Zig/Rust wasm lanes use.

name: GNU Make
recipe: N/A — Make's core function is to fork/exec recipe subprocesses (job.c built on vfork/exec/waitpid + pipe-based jobserver). wasip1 has no fork/exec/system/posix_spawn/pipe-jobcontrol. The parse/DAG core could compile under wasm32-wasi (Lane B C, pregenerated config), but a Make that cannot spawn recipe commands does nothing useful. Making it work requires a custom process-spawning shim that intercepts recipe execution and dispatches to in-sandbox wasm command invocations (CommandRegistry) — a bespoke host integration, not a plain wasm32-wasi build, and outside lanes A-D.
smoke: printf 'all:\n\techo hi\n' > Makefile && make  # would need fork/exec to run the 'echo hi' recipe — unsupported on wasip1
blocker: fork-exec: Make's purpose is forking/execing recipe subprocesses (vfork/exec/waitpid + pipe jobserver in job.c); wasip1 has no process spawning. Without a custom recipe-dispatch shim onto in-sandbox wasm commands, Make can parse but never run recipes.

name: Ninja
recipe: N/A — Ninja's job is to fork/exec build subprocesses in parallel (subprocess-posix.cc: posix_spawn + pipe + ppoll). Pure .ninja graph eval is real but inert without spawning child compilers. Same no-fork/exec wall as make. No standalone wasm32-wasi port exists. Would require a host-brokered subprocess->wasm-command bridge that does not exist.
smoke: N/A — cannot run a build without spawning subprocesses. If a bridge existed: `ninja --version` (pure, would print) then a 1-rule build.ninja whose `command` maps to an in-sandbox wasm command via the bridge.
blocker: fork-exec: Ninja exists solely to spawn parallel build subprocesses (posix_spawn/fork+exec, ppoll on pipes). No native exec in sandbox; no subprocess-to-wasm-command bridge. Graph eval is pure but does nothing alone.

name: OCaml / js_of_ocaml
recipe: No viable lane. (A) No prebuilt PLAIN wasm32-wasi ocamlc/ocamlrun runs under bare wasmtime. The two wasm OCaml toolchains both fail bare-wasmtime: wasm_of_ocaml emits WasmGC modules requiring GC + funcref + i31 + the exception-handling proposal — README confirms targets are Chrome/Node/Firefox/Safari only; none of wasm3/wasmer/wasmtime/wasmedge support that combo today. WasiCaml does target wasm32-unknown-wasi but its OCaml exception mechanism is implemented via JS exception handling, and the author states 'WasiCaml-produced code can so far not be run with wasmtime or wasmer.' ocamlrun.wasm (corwin-of-amber/ocaml-wasm) is built on wasi-kernel, browser-oriented, no evidence of standalone bare-wasmtime CLI operation. (B) Self-contained C lane is not feasible either: the OCaml system is a large autotools (configure/codegen) C runtime AND ocamlc is self-hosted OCaml that needs an existing OCaml bootstrap compiler to build — not a single :include_only/:compile_only amalgam. js_of_ocaml itself only emits JavaScript (no wasm artifact) so it is out of scope for a wasm command. Not Rust (C codebase), not pure-Python, not a QuickJS-shippable JS bundle.
smoke: N/A — cannot produce a wasm32-wasi module that runs under bare wasmtime. If one existed: printf '%s' 'print_string "hi\n"' > t.ml; wasmtime ocamlc.wasm -- t.ml -o t.byte; wasmtime ocamlrun.wasm -- t.byte  (expect: hi). Today this fails: wasm_of_ocaml output traps on missing GC/EH features in wasmtime; WasiCaml output traps on missing exception-handling imports.
blocker: wasm_of_ocaml requires WasmGC + funcref + i31 + exception-handling proposals not supported by standalone wasmtime (browser/Node-only); WasiCaml's exception machinery depends on JS host EH and explicitly does not run under wasmtime/wasmer; the OCaml runtime is a large autotools/configure C codebase whose compiler (ocamlc) is self-hosted OCaml needing a native bootstrap toolchain, so no self-contained C-amalgam (Lane B) build exists. js_of_ocaml emits only JavaScript, producing no wasm artifact.

name: Perl interpreter (perl)
recipe: zeroperl (github.com/6over3/zeroperl) builds Perl5 (default 5.42.0, configurable via PERL_VERSION) as a self-contained wasm32-wasi module using WASI SDK + wasi-libc, fully sandboxed (no fork/exec/network/threads; needs /dev/null and FS preopens). It is a genuine plain wasm32-wasi target, NOT emscripten/browser/js-pair — matching Lane A in spirit. CRITICAL CAVEAT: Perl's interpreter relies on setjmp/longjmp, and zeroperl compiles it with `-lsetjmp -mllvm -wasm-enable-sjlj`, which lowers SjLj onto the WASM exception-handling (exnref) proposal. At the time the author wrote it up, NO mainstream runtime (wasmtime/wasmer) supported exnref, so zeroperl only ran under toywasm and later WACS (a C# runtime). Since then (late-Mar→Aug 2025) wasmtime + Cranelift DID land a full exception-handling/exnref implementation, so the runtime gap is plausibly closed — but no one has demonstrated zeroperl running under wasmtime, and there is NO prebuilt .wasm release (build is a Docker/Apple-Container provision chain). To attempt: build the module via zeroperl's Docker recipe, then run `wasmtime run --dir=. zeroperl.wasm -- -e 'print "ok\n"'` on a current wasmtime with EH enabled.
smoke: wasmtime run --dir=::/dev/null --dir=. zeroperl.wasm -- -e 'print "hello from perl ".$]."\n"' # expect: hello from perl 5.042000
blocker: zeroperl proves Perl5 builds as a clean wasm32-wasi module (no fork/exec/net/threads), but its interpreter requires setjmp/longjmp lowered via `-mllvm -wasm-enable-sjlj` onto the WASM exception-handling (exnref) proposal. It was only ever validated under toywasm/WACS because wasmtime/wasmer lacked exnref. Wasmtime added full exception-handling/exnref support in 2025, so this MAY now run — but it is UNPROVEN on wasmtime, there is no prebuilt .wasm (heavy Docker build only), and the exact LLVM wasm-sjlj output may not match wasmtime's exnref ABI/encoding. Needs a build-and-run validation before claiming live-likely.

name: WAMR (WebAssembly Micro Runtime)
recipe: Lane B self-contained C/C++. Build ONLY the classic or fast interpreter (pure portable C, zero codegen): defines WASM_ENABLE_INTERP=1, WASM_ENABLE_JIT=0, WASM_ENABLE_AOT=0, WASM_ENABLE_FAST_JIT=0. Disable threads (WASM_ENABLE_LIB_PTHREAD=0, no wasi-threads) and sockets (no WASM_ENABLE_LIB_SOCKET) -> no native-thread/network deps. Use the posix platform layer (core/shared/platform/posix/*) which maps to wasi clocks/mmap-free alloc; select WASM_MEM_ALLOC via system_allocator (no mmap needed for interp). Target wasm32-wasi with our C/libc++ amalgam lane, substituting WAMR's config the mbedtls/freetype way (config header injection in place of CMake's generated platform/config headers) so no CMake configure run is required. Compile core/iwasm/interpreter + core/iwasm/common + shared/platform/posix + shared/utils + shared/mem-alloc/ems into one wasm32-wasi module. Embed via the standalone iwasm app (product-mini) reading a .wasm path and running its interpreter loop -> wasm-in-wasm, interpreted (slow but functional).
smoke: Compile a trivial guest add.wasm ((module (func (export "add") (param i32 i32)(result i32) local.get 0 local.get 1 i32.add))). Run the WAMR-interpreter wasm32-wasi module under wasmtime, passing add.wasm; have it instantiate, call add(2,3), assert result == 5 printed to stdout. Confirms interpreter-only build runs nested wasm with no JIT/threads/net.
blocker: Main risk is replacing CMake's generated platform/config headers with hand-injected config defines (config-substitution, same pattern as already-live mbedtls/freetype). EMS allocator must be set to a fixed-pool/system_allocator mode to avoid mmap. Interpreter is pure C with no codegen, no native threads, no network, no fork-exec -> none of the impossible triggers apply.

name: PostgreSQL
recipe: No viable lane. PostgreSQL is a fork()-based multi-process server (signals, shared memory, sockets) — none native to wasm. The only proven wasm slice is PGlite, which is an EMSCRIPTEN build (fails Lane A's no-emscripten/no-js-pair rule): it relies on browser/Node VFS shims and drives Postgres single-user mode through a JS I/O bridge, non-portable to wasmtime. A pure wasm32-wasi build is only EXPERIMENTAL and incomplete — blocked on Postgres's longjmp-based error handling (sigsetjmp/siglongjmp), which has no native WASM equivalent; emscripten supplies a workaround (asyncify) that a WASI build would have to reimplement natively, and it is not done. No prebuilt wasm32-wasi .wasm exists to download (Lane A fails). Lane B fails: Postgres is millions of LOC with autoconf/configure-generated headers, not an :include_only/:compile_only amalgam, and even single-user mode needs longjmp the host C lane can't satisfy. Lanes C/D n/a (C server, not Rust crate / pure-Python / QuickJS-JS). pglite-oxide's wasmtime claim is false — it ships a NATIVE pg 17.5 binary, not wasm. Embedded-SQL need is already served by LIVE sqlite3; Postgres-specific server is not portable to the sandbox.
smoke: N/A — cannot produce a wasm32-wasi .wasm. (Closest analog if a future WASI build landed: `postgres --single -D /pgdata postgres` fed `SELECT version();\nCREATE TABLE t(x int); INSERT INTO t VALUES(1); SELECT sum(x) FROM t;` on stdin, expecting the row result — but no such .wasm is runnable under wasmtime today.)
blocker: Only wasm slice (PGlite) is an emscripten/JS-paired build, not plain wasm32-wasi; the experimental WASI build is incomplete, blocked on longjmp error-handling with no native WASM equivalent. Plus fork/multi-process server model unsupported. No prebuilt standalone .wasm and not amalgam-compilable from C source.

name: Redis
recipe: No viable recipe to ship Redis-as-described. Redis's purpose is a networked in-memory store/broker: clients speak RESP over TCP sockets; OS coupling is the ae event loop (epoll/kqueue), listening sockets, and fork()-for-RDB/AOF persistence. None of those survive plain wasm32-wasi (no sockets-as-server, no fork, no threads). The ONLY thing that compiles (Fluence's research port) is a gutted request/response command-eval core with networking, persistence, cluster, background threads, and the event loop ALL stripped out — i.e. an embedded KV library, not Redis the server/broker. That is a fork, not a maintained prebuilt artifact, and overlaps capabilities we already ship (sqlite3 + lua + in-memory structures).
smoke: N/A — would-be smoke (redis-server --port 0 then PING/SET/GET over a socket) is unreachable: no server sockets in wasm32-wasi sandbox. Even the stripped port exposes only a synchronous command-eval entrypoint, not the RESP server contract that defines Redis.
blocker: Network-purpose: Redis IS a networked server (RESP over TCP sockets, remote clients, pub/sub broker) — server sockets + ae event loop + fork()-for-persistence have no plain wasm32-wasi/wasmtime equivalent. The only buildable subset (Fluence fork) deletes networking/persistence/threads/event-loop, yielding an embedded KV lib that is not Redis-the-store/broker and duplicates sqlite3+lua we already ship.

name: Valkey
recipe: N/A — cannot build as in-sandbox wasm32-wasi. Valkey is a network-server daemon (Redis fork), not an embeddable library. Core couples to: TCP/Unix-socket listeners + ae event loop (whole purpose is serving clients over the network), fork()-based BGSAVE/persistence and copy-on-write, background threads (bio, optional IO threads), and jemalloc as default allocator. None of fork(), sockets-as-purpose, or threads exist under plain wasm32-wasi/wasmtime. No library/embedded mode, no WASI target. Lua is already covered live via the existing lua engine; KV storage is already covered live via sqlite3.
smoke: N/A — no buildable artifact. (Hypothetical disproof: `valkey-server --port 0` would immediately need socket bind + event loop; a SET/GET roundtrip requires a client connecting over a socket, which is unavailable in-sandbox.)
blocker: network-purpose daemon: requires sockets/event-loop (raison d'être), fork() for BGSAVE+COW persistence, and background threads — none available under plain wasm32-wasi/wasmtime; no embeddable library mode, no WASI port. Same profile as Redis. KV need already covered live by sqlite3; scripting by lua.

name: BadgerDB
recipe: Lane A (Go GOOS=wasip1 AOT). BadgerDB is pure-Go no-cgo, but depends on github.com/dgraph-io/ristretto/v2/z for memory-mapping. In ristretto z/mmap_wasip1.go (//go:build wasip1), mmap/munmap/madvise/msync are HARD STUBS returning syscall.ENOSYS. Badger opens every persistent SST table and value-log file via z.OpenMmapFile -> OpenMmapFileUsing -> Mmap(); on Mmap error it returns immediately with NO non-mmap fallback. So an on-disk (durable) Badger DB.Open fails at first table/vlog open under wasip1. Only WithInMemory(true) avoids mmap, but that is an ephemeral non-durable store -- not the embeddable persistent LSM the package exists to provide. Compilation to wasip1 succeeds; runtime durable operation does not.
smoke: GOOS=wasip1 GOARCH=wasm go build a tiny main that does badger.Open(badger.DefaultOptions("/tmp/db")) then a Set+Get+View; run the .wasm under wasmtime --dir=/tmp. Expect failure at Open: 'function not implemented' (ENOSYS) wrapped 'while mmapping .../000001.vlog' from ristretto z. With badger.DefaultOptions("").WithInMemory(true) it would Set/Get but writes nothing to disk -- proving only the non-durable mode runs.
blocker: Durable path needs mmap; ristretto z/mmap_wasip1.go returns syscall.ENOSYS and Badger's table/vlog open has no non-mmap fallback (only ephemeral WithInMemory mode survives). dir_other.go also disables file locking. Persistent embeddable KV store -- the product -- is non-functional on wasm32-wasi.

name: BoltDB / bbolt
recipe: No viable lane. bbolt is pure-Go, so our Lane-B (C/C++) and Lane-C (mrustc Rust) and Lane-D (Python/JS) do not apply; the only route is Go's own GOOS=wasip1 backend (Lane-A prebuilt plain wasm32-wasi). But upstream has NO wasip1/wasm/js platform file (root has only bolt_aix/android/linux/openbsd/solaris/unix/windows.go), and the storage engine is fundamentally mmap-based: bolt_unix.go calls syscall.Mmap(MAP_SHARED) for the DB file and flock() for the lock. wasip1 provides neither mmap nor flock, so `GOOS=wasip1 GOARCH=wasm go build` fails to compile / link. Making it run requires a non-trivial fork that replaces the mmap'd page access with a read()/pread-backed buffer and stubs locking — a real port, not a config flip. No prebuilt plain wasm32-wasi .wasm exists upstream.
smoke: After a hypothetical mmap-eliminated port: bbolt CLI under wasmtime — `bbolt.wasm` create test.db, open a writable bucket, Put(key,val), reopen DB from a fresh wasmtime instance (file persisted to a preopened dir), Get(key) returns val, and `bbolt check test.db` reports a consistent B+tree. None of this is reachable today because upstream does not compile for wasip1.
blocker: Storage engine is fundamentally mmap+flock based (syscall.Mmap MAP_SHARED in bolt_unix.go); wasip1 has neither mmap nor flock and bbolt ships no wasip1/wasm platform file, so GOOS=wasip1 build fails. No upstream read()-backed fallback exists; running it needs a real port, not packaging. Also outside our C/Rust/Python/JS lanes (it's Go).

name: Berkeley DB
recipe: Lane B (self-contained C, same shape as the already-live sqlite3 but heavier). BDB is a mature ANSI/POSIX C library, in-process, no network/fork/threads/JIT/GPU required. Compile its core .c set (btree/, db/, mp/, os/, mutex/, optional txn/) with the live clang wasm32-wasi lane. Config is header-driven (db_config.h + db.h generated from db.in) — substitute a pregenerated config a la MBEDTLS_CONFIG_FILE, since the autoconf dist/configure cannot run in-sandbox. Build single-threaded: select the no-shared-memory / simple mutex path (avoid mut_fcntl.c and mut_pthread.c; use a test-and-set or no-op stub). Avoid mmap and POSIX fcntl env-locking by running env in DB_PRIVATE mode (malloc-backed region, no env mmap) plus DB_ENV set_flags DB_NOMMAP for DB files. OS layer (os_open/os_rw/os_truncate) maps onto wasip1 open/pread/pwrite/ftruncate, all present. Replication/RPC stay compiled out (off by default).
smoke: Single-threaded C: db_env_create then DB_ENV open on /tmp/bdbenv with DB_CREATE|DB_INIT_MPOOL|DB_PRIVATE; db_create; DB set_flags DB_NOMMAP; DB open BTREE t.db with DB_CREATE; put 3 key/value DBTs; get them back and assert values match; close DB and env. Then reopen env+db and get the keys again to assert persistence across reopen. Exit 0 if all match.
blocker: No pre-shipped amalgamation (unlike sqlite3): must assemble the .c set and substitute a pregenerated db_config.h/db.h because autoconf configure cannot run in-sandbox. Must select a single-thread mutex path (no shared-memory/fcntl/pthread mutexes) and run DB_PRIVATE + DB_NOMMAP to avoid env mmap and POSIX advisory file locking (absent in wasip1). With those set it is pure in-process POSIX C; risk is config/mutex-path assembly effort, not a hard impossibility.

name: ripgrep (rg)
recipe: No viable lane. Lane A: no official/prebuilt plain wasm32-wasi .wasm exists upstream (only unofficial emscripten/wasm-pack experiments). Lane C (bare Rust via mrustc~1.74) is impossible: Cargo.toml declares edition=2024 and rust-version=1.85.0 (verified from raw Cargo.toml on master), far beyond mrustc's ~1.74/edition-2018-2021 ceiling. It also pulls serde_derive/serde proc-macros, the regex + aho-corasick crates (build-script-generated DFA/SIMD tables), crossbeam for native-thread parallelism, and memmap-based search — each independently fatal for mrustc. Lanes B (C/C++) and D (Python/JS) do not apply (it is Rust). Capability is also largely already covered live by pcre2(grep)+coreutils.
smoke: N/A — no buildable artifact. If a plain wasm32-wasi .wasm ever existed: printf 'foo\nBAR baz\n' > /tmp/t.txt && wasmtime run --dir /tmp rg.wasm -i bar /tmp/t.txt  (expect line 'BAR baz' matched). Note rg uses native threads (crossbeam) + mmap dir-walk, so even a hypothetical build needs single-thread + WASI fd-based fallback.
blocker: Rust edition 2024 + MSRV 1.85.0 (verified in master Cargo.toml) exceed mrustc ~1.74; plus serde_derive proc-macros, regex/aho-corasick build-script codegen, and crossbeam native-thread parallelism. No prebuilt plain wasm32-wasi .wasm upstream. Not C/C++/Python/JS, so lanes A/B/D unavailable. (Capability mostly already live via pcre2 grep + coreutils.)

name: ag (The Silver Searcher)
recipe: Lane B (self-contained C) is the only candidate path, but requires a heavy fork, not a clean compile. Steps if attempted: (1) pregenerate autotools (run ./build.sh + ./configure on a native host, vendor the generated config.h/Makefile to bypass configure in-sandbox); (2) rip out the Pthreads worker pool — ag's parallel search is its core architecture (work_queue + worker threads in search.c/main.c); replace with a single-threaded sequential file walk. WASI has no native threads (impossible per rules), so threading must be removed, not shimmed; (3) build PCRE with JIT disabled (interpreted mode) — ag links PCRE's JIT compiler explicitly; or retarget onto already-live pcre2; (4) shim mmap() — ag mmap()s every searched file; wasi-libc only supports MAP_ANONYMOUS, so file mmap must fall back to read-into-buffer (patch decompress.c/search.c); (5) zlib + lzma needed for -z compressed search — buildable (compress libs already live) or stub out. Net: not a port that survives as plain wasm32-wasi without rewriting ag's concurrency model.
smoke:
printf 'foo
needle here
bar
' > /tmp/t.txt && ag needle /tmp/t.txt  # expect: line 2 match "needle here" printed with line number
blocker: Core architecture is multithreaded (Pthreads worker pool is HOW ag searches) — native threads are impossible under wasmtime, so threading must be surgically removed, not compiled. PCRE links its JIT compiler (needs --disable-jit or retarget to live pcre2), and ag mmap()s every file (WASI lacks file-backed mmap, needs read-buffer shim). Each is fixable but together they constitute a substantial fork, not a self-contained compile. Also largely REDUNDANT: pcre2grep is already LIVE and covers the grep/code-search use case.

name: bash
recipe: No viable recipe. Every working bash-on-wasm build (Wasmer's bash, WebAssembly.sh) is compiled against WASIX, Wasmer's POSIX superset that adds fork/vfork/exec/posix_spawn/threads/job-control. WASIX is a Wasmer-runtime-only extension; wasmtime does not implement it. Plain wasm32-wasi preview1 has NO process model: no fork, no exec, no posix_spawn, no pipe-to-child, no ptys/job control. A shell's entire value is spawning external commands (fork+exec), pipelines, and job control — none expressible in preview1. No plain wasm32-wasi (non-WASIX, non-emscripten) bash port exists. A theoretical stub build (builtins only, fork/exec returning ENOSYS) would require the full autoconf/configure-generated build (lane B, heavy) and would still be unable to run any external command (ls/grep/cat) or pipe — i.e. not a usable shell. Not worth pursuing.
smoke: N/A — cannot produce a functional shell under plain wasm32-wasi/wasmtime. A hypothetical builtins-only build would at most run `echo "$((1+2))"` with zero external-command/pipe capability, which is not a shell.
blocker: fork-exec: bash requires fork/exec/posix_spawn/pipes/job-control to run external commands and pipelines; plain wasm32-wasi preview1 has no process model. The only working wasm bash builds depend on WASIX (Wasmer-only, not wasmtime). No non-WASIX plain-wasi bash port exists.

name: fd
recipe: No viable lane. Lane C (mrustc ~1.74) blocked: edition 2024 unparseable, MSRV 1.77.2 above ceiling, clap derive proc-macro impossible. No prebuilt wasm (Lane A). Not C/C++ (B) or Python/JS (D).
smoke: Run fd to match rs files in a WASI-preopened dir with a.rs, b.txt, sub/c.rs; expect the two rs paths on stdout.
blocker: edition 2024 + MSRV 1.77.2 + clap derive proc-macro exceed mrustc ~1.74; no prebuilt wasm.
